summary: Iteration 5: Backend 26/26 passed (bootstrap, geo, categories, order filters/lifecycle, proposals, chat, favorites, reports, notifications, admin + 403). Frontend E2E (onboarding → home → mode switch → create wizard 6 steps → publish → worker proposal → client accept → chat → start → complete → review) executed end-to-end successfully on 390x844. Two frontend bugs found: (1) Admin 'Categorias' section crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading map)' at admin.tsx:143 when leaking previous section's data (orders/users arrays) during section switch — this also blocks reaching Localidades/Denúncias sections in the same session; (2) order detail duplicates the 'Quem pediu' block for non-owner viewers on published orders because two conditional blocks both render.

ui_bugs.issue: Race between section change and pending API responses lets non-category arrays (users/orders) flow into <Categories data={data} />, causing cat.subcategories.map to throw. Guard should also validate shape (e.g., data.every(c => Array.isArray(c.subcategories))) or cancel stale requests. Reference: /app/frontend/app/admin.tsx:92,143

Duplicate 'Quem pediu' section renders for non-owner when order has no worker. Line 193 already covers order.client for !isOwner (renders 'Quem pediu' with otherUser=order.client) and lines 199-204 render another 'Quem pediu' with order.client. Reference: /app/frontend/app/order/[id].tsx:193-204

integration_issues.issue: After Categoria crash the entire admin route dies; subsequent Localidades/Denúncias chips are not clickable. Users must reload.

issues: Client card shown twice under identical 'Quem pediu' headings — confusing for the worker before sending proposal.

react_native_issues.issue: Console reports 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents' and '"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow"' — from RN 0.79/expo-router internals; low priority but noise in logs.

action_items: Fix /app/frontend/app/admin.tsx: guard Categories rendering with Array.isArray(data) && data.every(c => Array.isArray(c.subcategories)); ideally cancel/tag stale requests via a section ref or React Query.
Fix /app/frontend/app/order/[id].tsx: remove the redundant second 'Quem pediu' block at lines 199-204 (already covered by line 193's !isOwner branch).
Optional: replace deprecated pointerEvents and shadow* style usages if reachable in app code (mostly upstream).
critical_code_review_comments: Admin panel does not debounce/cancel per-section fetches, so section-mismatched arrays can be shoved into the category renderer.
OrderDetail has overlapping conditional blocks for the client card; both fire for the same state (non-owner, no worker).

Order detail Star review UI was not encountered during the E2E — the mutual review submission via API is tested and passes, but a manual reload was necessary to see the stars UI after completion in the same session; consider explicit navigation/refetch after complete_order.

success_rate.frontend: ≈85% (E2E happy path passes; admin categories crash and duplicated client card are the only failures)

seed_data_creation: Backend test suite created TEST_<uuid> orders, proposal, review, chat message, favorite, report, and a throwaway cancelled order. All labelled with TAG. No cleanup endpoint exists.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Public URL: https://faze-fazedores.preview.emergentagent.com. Onboarding stored in localStorage 'faze:onboarded' — set it before tests to skip. Segmented control uses testIDs segment-client / segment-worker. Star testIDs are star-1..star-5. Activity 'Meus serviços' tab uses testID activity-tab-jobs (not -services).
rca_of_issue: Admin categories crash RCA: /app/frontend/app/admin.tsx line 38 uses `useEffect(() => { setData(null); load(); }, [load])` where load() is section-scoped. When the user taps section chips faster than the previous request settles, an older section's response wins the setData race. Line 92 only checks Array.isArray(data), and both /admin/users and /admin/orders return arrays; when they leak into <Categories data={data}/>, line 143 `cat.subcategories.map(...)` explodes because those objects don't have subcategories. Fix: (a) also verify data.every(item => Array.isArray(item.subcategories)) before rendering Categories, and/or (b) tag each fetch with the section and drop responses whose section != current.
